d: Indonesia has passed a landmark asset forfeiture law, allowing authorities to seize certain assets linked to criminal activity without first securing a conviction. The legislation comes after 18 years of debate and is intended to strengthen the country's fight against corruption and other serious offences. In this video, Firstpost explains how the new law works, the conditions under which assets can be confiscated and how victims of fraudulent investment schemes could receive compensation.
